To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the dilution effect must be rigorously taken into account to obtain exact TC equations and (ii) a one-step association mechanism is thermodynamically equivalent (i.e. can explain the same TC) to an infinite number of multi-step mechanisms, and thus can never be excluded by a single TC.

(1) the exact equations of titration calorimetric curves can be derived, and that (2) the multi-step mechanisms that are equivalent to the single-step association/dissocation mechanism are not only theoretically equivalent but also practically equivalent, in the sense that the same titration curve can be explained with either mechanism.
(i) the exact equations for ITC titration curves (with multi-injections or continuous injections) are derived, and (ii) they are incorporated in AFFINImeter, a software for the analysis of ITC data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
rigorous mathematical and physical analysis of ITC experiments.
the development of new theoretical tools for processing ITC data and with their application to various practical problems in biochemistry and biophysics.
a better understanding of the physical meaning of the parameters used in ITC and the mathematical methods to obtain them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the one-step association mechanism, the ITC data are compatible with a unique set of parameters (K d and ΔH), while the data are compatible with an infinite number of sets of parameters for any multi-step equivalent mechanisms.
a sigmoid TC is the only experimental proof of a one-step mechanism.
the ITC data can only be explained by the one-step association/ dissociation mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ITC is a very robust and powerful technique for measuring thermodynamic parameters, but that it is not a good method for elucidating reaction mechanisms.
the ITC data analysis must be performed with the rigorous mathematical equations, and not with approximate equations.
the rigorous equations derived here, together with the exact equations for the dilution effect, are the only equations that can be used for processing ITC data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exact equations are needed for the analysis of ITC data.
ITC is a powerful technique to study protein-ligand interactions but that the analysis of TC should be done with great care, and the use of a dedicated software is highly recommended.
, contrary to what is commonly believed, the ITC method is not a “direct” technique.
